facts.fact: The article's alt-text bar chart of customer discovery channels labels Discovery at 75%.
facts.quote: Bar chart showing customer discovery channels: Discovery 75%, Direct (approx. 45%), Direct 50%, and Branded 30%.

facts.fact: A 'Direct' search in GBP Insights is when someone types in the business name.
facts.quote: understanding the difference between a "**Direct**" search (someone typed in your business name) and a "**Discovery**" search

facts.fact: A 'Discovery' search in GBP Insights is when someone searches for a category or service, such as 'plumber near me', without a specific business in mind.
facts.quote: a "**Discovery**" search (someone searched for a category, like "plumber near me")

facts.fact: The article states that when comparing ad impact on business outcomes, one should examine ad exposure, website activity, and completed actions separately and use documented data and an appropriate comparison period before attributing outcomes to advertising.
facts.quote: examine ad exposure, website activity, and completed actions separately. Use documented data and an appropriate comparison period before attributing a business outcome to advertising.

facts.fact: The article was published on March 20, 2026.
According to the page, website clicks account for 48% of all Google Business Profile actions, more than phone calls (21%) or directions (9%).
facts.quote: website clicks account for a massive **48%** of all GBP actions, way more than phone calls (**21%**) or directions (**9%**)

facts.fact: According to the page, phone calls account for 21% of Google Business Profile actions.
facts.quote: way more than phone calls (**21%**) or directions (**9%**)

facts.fact: The page states that businesses with complete Google Business Profiles can see up to 7x more clicks.
facts.quote: businesses with complete profiles can see up to **7x more clicks**

facts.fact: The page states that Google drives over 2 billion connections for businesses every month.
facts.quote: With Google driving over **2 billion** connections for businesses every month

facts.fact: The page says that a profile with just one photo gets ignored compared to one with ten or more photos.
facts.quote: A profile with just one photo gets ignored compared to one with ten or more.

facts.fact: The page says businesses with over 10 photos get far more attention on their profiles, based on what the Adwave team has seen.
facts.quote: We've seen that businesses with over **10** photos get way more attention.

facts.fact: The page recommends capturing baseline Google Business Profile metrics for the 30 days before an Adwave TV campaign airs.
facts.quote: Capture your key GBP metrics for the **30 days**_before_ your Adwave campaign hits the airwaves

facts.fact: The page recommends continuing to track the same Google Business Profile metrics for 30-60 days after ads start running.
facts.quote: Once your ads are running, keep tracking those same metrics for the next **30-60 days**.

facts.fact: The page recommends a monthly review of Google Business Profile Insights for most businesses.
facts.quote: For most businesses, a monthly review of your **Google Business Profile Insights** is the sweet spot.

facts.fact: The page recommends weekly checks of Google Business Profile Insights right after launching a new TV ad campaign or making major profile updates.
facts.quote: In that case, checking in weekly lets you see the immediate results and confirm whether your efforts are boosting key metrics

facts.fact: The page suggests year-over-year comparison, such as comparing April of the current year to April of the prior year, to separate growth from seasonality.
facts.quote: By comparing this April to last April, you can finally answer the question: "Are we growing, or are we just riding the usual seasonal wave?"
